title: November 11: native setpoint excitation (V26) and the proposed V27 cable/ring branch
summary: GeometricNeuronOriginReview is an archival causal review, not a numbered implementation. SurfaceListener (informally V26) reuses the audited feedback oscillator to study state-dependent surface listening, endogenous setpoint-port excitation, constant-dependent operating regimes, and a reliable but hand-wired one-way relay; the same setup does not yet learn, provide true refractory protection, or demonstrate persistent information. GeometricNeuronV27 exists as a repository and proposed spatial/ring continuation, but had only a licence at the time of review: its ring, memory, cable and growth mechanisms are untested hypotheses.

nodes.claim: Informal 'V26': a ten-round continuation of the audited Perception Lab geometric feedback loop, using moving checkerboard coupling and the original Homeostatic Coupler setpoint_mod input to study inter-unit excitation, oscillator/relay operating regimes and one-way transmission.
nodes.survived: With setpoint_mod open, the reduced native.py returns the original loop when uncoupled (parity test), and an arriving two-tap signal can elicit a receiver-generated beat without output override. At constant 1.6, otherwise silent followers relayed a one-way chain at weight -6 with 300/300 reaches and 4 ticks per hop; an eight-unit chain relayed 50/50 observed beats. The constant sweep finds self-beating and silent-but-excitable regimes. These are source-reported code/test results, not independent Genealogy reruns.
nodes.killed: The checkerboard's apparent special spatial code has not been isolated from scalar square-size dynamics. Moving-surface coupling could silence a colony, and merely removing the isolated-unit saw worsened it. The one-way chain uses hand-set constants and weights, bidirectional wiring runs away, and the silent relay responds without an absolute refractory period. No endogenous learning, long-term memory, physical dendritic cable or biological neuron has been established.
nodes.era: November 11: setpoint excitation and proposed spatial cables

nodes.claim: Newly created continuation proposed for spatially delayed/attenuated wiring and a circulating ring of silent geometric-neuron relays. The initial hypothesis is that a pulse may circulate without a separate oscillator; no implementation had been committed when this note was written.
nodes.survived: The repository exists and the proposed experiment follows from V26's demonstrated one-way event regeneration. No V27 experimental success is recorded yet.
nodes.killed: A persistent ring, stable multi-pulse patterns, erase, increased capacity with longer cables, and selective excitation by distance have not been tested. A one-way loop is not automatically reliable memory: pulses can collide or cause repeated excitation, and finite propagation timing/recovery must be measured. Physical cable biophysics and learning are not implemented.

edges.why: SurfaceListener's gn/core.py retains the reduced 59-tick ECG colony from the ReturnToGeometricNeuron work, while native.py reopens the original setpoint_mod port and the later coupling/receptor experiments are declared additions.

The archived origin-review graph and causal reconstruction are the reference for SurfaceListener's ten-round studies; the review itself is an audit and preservation repository, not a new physical neuron generation.

motifs.title: Native excitability and event relaying do not by themselves create stored information
motifs.description: A fixed homeostatic coupler changes from spontaneous clock to excitable relay as its setpoint constant changes. The sender's beat can drive the receiver through a port already present in the original graph, yet one-way transmission with manual weights, runaway bidirectional excitation and loss of activity when the input stops do not establish learning or persistent memory. The V27 ring is a proposed next falsification, not a measured successor mechanism.
